Τρῐκάρᾱνος [κᾰ], ὁ,
A.the Three-headed, a satirical attack on three cities, Sparta, Athens, and Thebes, written by Anaximenes of Lampsacus ( Frr. 20 and 21
J. ) and ascribed by him to Theopompus, Paus. 6.18.5 , Luc. Pseudol. 29 , Fug. 32 ; also a satire by Varro on the coalition of Caesar, Pompeius, and Crassus, App. BC 2.9 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
